subtopic: Mob and crowd behaviour (stampede, riot, online pile-on)
passage:
Sabina: Hey. I saw the thread. You don't have to explain anything.
Tanvir: I can't stop reading it. Two thousand comments about my talk.
Sabina: Okay. Can we do one thing? Mute the thread and turn notifications off for tonight. I'll stay on this chat.
Tanvir: What if it gets worse
Sabina: Then we deal with it together. I've saved the ones that are plain abuse and I'll report them from my side too. You don't have to look at them.
Tanvir: Rohan posted a joke about it. Meher liked it. Kunal hasn't said anything at all.
Sabina: That's on them. I'm bringing dinner at 8. Just food, no talking about it unless you want to.
Tanvir: ok. thank you
Sabina: I'm here till you fall asleep.

qa.q: At what time is Sabina bringing dinner?
Why might Tanvir keep reading the thread even though it hurts?
qa.a: Tanvir feels exposed and may fear missing the next comment, so reading feels unavoidable even though it deepens the hurt.

qa.q: What did Sabina suggest first to help Tanvir?
qa.a: Sabina suggested muting the thread and turning notifications off for the night while staying on the chat.

qa.q: What might Sabina be feeling while promising to stay on the chat till Tanvir falls asleep?
qa.a: Sabina is probably worried about Tanvir and protective, which is why Sabina saves and reports the abusive comments and plans to bring dinner at 8.

grounding: Someone messages the target of a pile-on privately, helps them stop reading comments and reports the abuse, offering steady human contact.

passage:
By evening every phone in town had the clip of Anirban stumbling over the welcome speech at the school function. Jatin found him on the roof of the tuition centre, phone in his hand, thumb still scrolling. “Give it here for a bit,” Jatin said quietly, and Anirban did. Jatin switched off the comments, then sat on the parapet beside him with two cups of tea from the stall below.

Down there a few boys were still laughing at the clip. Pintu looked away as Jatin passed.

“Let's not read it tonight,” Jatin said. Later he helped Anirban report the cruellest messages and block the accounts. When Anirban's mother called up the stairs for dinner, Jatin went down with him. “I'll walk you to school tomorrow.” Anirban nodded, eyes on his tea.

qa.a: Jatin found Anirban on the roof of the tuition centre.

qa.q: What does Anirban's nod with eyes on the tea suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Anirban is tired and hurt but grateful, quietly accepting company because words are hard.

qa.q: What steps did Jatin take to help besides staying nearby?
qa.a: Jatin switched off the comments, helped Anirban report the cruellest messages and block the accounts.

qa.q: What might Pintu feel while looking away as Jatin passes?
qa.a: Pintu might feel a flicker of guilt or embarrassment about laughing at the clip, and also worry about being the next target.

grounding: A person helps the target of an online pile-on stop reading comments, reports abuse and stays close, valuing steady contact over public defence.
